name: Poland
summary: Warsaw's stock market tradition goes back to 1817, but today's Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW) was re-founded in 1991 after the end of communism. In 2018 FTSE Russell promoted Poland to developed-market status. The WIG20 tracks 20 large companies, led by banks, energy and retail. Shares trade in Polish złoty.

currency.name: Polish złoty
currency.note: Poland is in the EU but not in the euro area, so a euro investor carries currency risk: moves of the złoty against the euro change the value of Polish shares in euros (Category L).

source.title: FTSE Equity Country Classification Process, v3.5, October 2026, Appendix 3 (FTSE Russell, PDF)

exchanges.name: Warsaw Stock Exchange (Giełda Papierów Wartościowych, GPW)
exchanges.founded: 1991 (company founded on 12 April 1991); market traditions since 1817
exchanges.hours: For shares in continuous trading: orders for the opening auction from 08:30, opening price at 09:00, continuous trading 09:00–16:50, closing auction 16:50–17:00, then trading at the closing price until 17:05. Less liquid shares trade in single-price auctions instead.
exchanges.note: GPW also runs NewConnect, a market for smaller companies, and the bond market Catalyst.

indexes.name: WIG20
indexes.description: Calculated since 16 April 1994 from 20 major and most liquid companies on the WSE Main List. Calculated by GPW Benchmark.

regulators.name: Polish Financial Supervision Authority (KNF)
regulators.role: Supervises the Polish financial market, including banks, insurers, investment firms and the capital market.

investorProtection.name: Bank Guarantee Fund (BFG)
investorProtection.text: Eligible deposits at banks and cooperative credit unions, in złoty or foreign currencies, are covered up to €100,000 per depositor and institution.

settlement.cycle: T+2 (two business days); T+1 from 11 October 2027
settlement.csd: KDPW (Krajowy Depozyt Papierów Wartościowych), the central securities depository
settlement.note: As an EU member, Poland moves to next-day settlement on 11 October 2027.

source.title: One year to go for T+1 settlement (ESMA, 16 October 2026)

rules.title: Short selling (EU rules)
rules.text: Net short positions in shares must be reported to the regulator from 0.1% of issued share capital and published from 0.5% (Category N).

taxes.glance: Residents: 19% flat tax on gains from selling shares (declared on PIT-38) and on dividends. Non-residents can apply the rate of a double taxation agreement under conditions.

items.title: Capital gains (residents)
items.text: Income from selling shares and other securities is taxed at 19%, declared on the PIT-38 return. Losses can be offset against income from the same source in the following five years, within limits.

items.title: Dividends
items.text: Dividends and other profit shares are subject to a 19% flat-rate tax.

items.title: Non-residents
items.text: People with limited tax liability in Poland can apply the rate from a double taxation agreement, under conditions set by Polish law.

items.title: For an Austrian investor
items.text: An Austrian bank can credit foreign withholding tax up to 15% of the dividend against Austrian KESt (Category Q).

sources.title: Broszura do PIT-38 za 2025 r. (Ministry of Finance, podatki.gov.pl, PDF, in Polish)

access: Some Austrian banks and brokers offer trading on the Warsaw Stock Exchange; check currency conversion into złoty.
Indirectly, through funds or ETFs on Polish or emerging/eastern European indexes (Category H).

history.text: The Warsaw Mercantile Exchange is established.
After the fall of communism, the Warsaw Stock Exchange company is founded on 12 April by the State Treasury.
The WIG20 index is first calculated, on 16 April.
FTSE Russell promotes Poland to developed-market status (effective 24 September 2018).

funFacts: Poland was promoted by FTSE Russell step by step: from Secondary Emerging to Advanced Emerging in 2008, and to Developed in 2018.
